name: Shiftline
brief:
# Shiftline — Office Shift & Appointment Scheduler

## What this is
An internal tool for scheduling office shifts and appointments. A manager builds
a weekly rota for staff and books rooms for appointments; staff see their own
upcoming shifts and any conflicts are surfaced before they happen.

## Users
- **Manager** — builds the rota, assigns shifts, books appointments.
- **Staff** — view their own shifts and request time off.
- **Reception** — books appointments into rooms.

## Core domain
- **Staff**: id, name, role, weekly hour cap, active.
- **Room**: id, name, capacity, active.
- **Shift**: id, staff, date, start time, end time, role note.
- **Appointment**: id, title, room, date, start time, end time, booked-by,
  attendee count (must not exceed room capacity).
- **TimeOffRequest**: id, staff, start date, end date, status (Requested |
  Approved | Denied), note.

## Required features
1. **Weekly rota** — a 7-day grid (Monday–Sunday) with shifts per day per staff.
   Add a shift by picking staff, date, start, end. Refuse overlapping shifts for
   the same staff member on the same day.
2. **Hour cap check** — when a shift would push a staff member over their weekly
   hour cap, warn and refuse (or allow with an explicit override flag); show the
   running weekly hours per staff.
3. **Appointments** — book an appointment into a room; refuse double-booking the
   same room at overlapping times and refuse attendee count over room capacity.
4. **Conflict detector** — a screen that scans the week and lists every hard
   conflict (double-booked room, overlapping staff shift, shift overlapping
   approved time off) with the two offending entries named.
5. **Staff view** — pick a staff member and see their shifts for the current week
   plus approved/denied time off.
6. **Time off** — request time off; manager approves or denies with a note. An
   approved time-off range that overlaps an existing shift is flagged in the
   conflict detector.

## Functional requirements
- Times are stored as minutes-from-midnight integers per date; durations and
  overlaps are computed from integers (exact, no timezone ambiguity).
- Overlap rule: two intervals overlap iff startA < endB && startB < endA.
- Weekly hours sum shift durations against the staff cap.
- All conflict checks are pure functions over the schedule data, unit-testable,
  and reused by both the rota builder and the conflict screen.
- Refusals name the specific conflicting entry.

## Non-functional requirements
- Desktop-first, usable to 1024px; keyboard-navigable grid.
- Accessible: labelled time inputs, table/grid roles where appropriate.
- Deterministic scheduling logic separated from UI.
- Local persistence; no external calendar integration required.

## Explicitly out of scope
- Google/Outlook calendar sync.
- Recurring shifts or RRULE expansion.
- Payroll calculations from hours.
- Notifications by email/SMS.

artifacts.title: Phase narrative (LLM)
artifacts.body:
**P0 Deep Research & Feasibility — Shiftline**

Research confirms a validated, urgent problem space: 2026 A&E benchmarks show a widening gap between technical capability and operational efficiency, with firms billing only 81% of staff time and 1 in 3 architecture practices spending less than half their hours on design—admin burden, not capability, is the bottleneck. Absence tracking and shift infrastructure are flagged as non-negotiable compliance vectors for 2026, mandating unified absence and rota visibility where rota creation natively reads from leave data, and AI adoption plus flexible-work strategies are actively reshaping how AE teams are scheduled. Critically, no dominant incumbent serves the *internal office* shift-and-appointment use case; existing tools split between enterprise workforce management (overbuilt for SMB A&E) and generic calendars (no conflict detection, no absence integration). Feasibility is high: the core build—weekly rota CRUD, per-staff shift views, room booking, and pre-emptive conflict surfacing—is achievable with standard web-stack patterns, and the unified absence/rota visibility requirement is a data-model concern, not a research risk. The open questions are scoping ones: whether to model appointments and shifts as one unified availability primitive or two linked entities, and how much of the 2026 compliance surface (leave accrual rules, working-time directives) must ship in v1 versus v2. Verdict: **feasible, well-timed, and narrowly scoped—proceed to P1 requirements definition**, with the unified-availability data model and compliance floor as the first decisions to lock.

requirements: Provide a 7-day rota grid (Monday through Sunday) rendering shifts per day per staff member, navigable by keyboard and usable down to 1024px width.

Allow adding a shift by picking staff, date, start time, and end time, where times are stored as minutes-from-midnight integers per date and durations/overlaps are computed from those integers with no timezone conversion.
Refuse a shift that overlaps an existing shift for the same staff member on the same day using the rule startA < endB && startB < endA, naming the specific conflicting shift entry in the refusal.
Compute and display running weekly hours per staff member by summing that staff member's shift durations for the Monday–Sunday week.

When adding a shift would push a staff member over their weekly hour cap, warn and refuse by default, while allowing the shift only when an explicit override flag is set; expose whether the override was used.
Book an appointment into a room with title, room, date, start time, end time, booked-by, and attendee count, refusing bookings where the attendee count exceeds the room capacity.
Refuse an appointment that double-books the same room at overlapping times using startA < endB && startB < endA, naming the specific conflicting appointment.

Provide a conflict detector screen that scans the week and lists every hard conflict — double-booked room, overlapping staff shift, and shift overlapping approved time off — with both offending entries named for each conflict.
Provide a staff view where selecting a staff member shows that member's shifts for the current week plus that member's approved and denied time off requests.
Allow a staff member to request time off with a start date, end date, and note, and allow a manager to approve or deny it with a note, updating status to Approved or Denied.
Flag an approved time-off range that overlaps an existing shift in the conflict detector, naming both the shift and the time-off request.

Persist staff, rooms, shifts, appointments, and time-off requests locally with no external calendar integration, and keep all conflict/hours/overlap logic as pure functions separate from the UI and reusable by both the rota builder and the conflict screen.
edgeCases: A shift added with start time equal to another shift's end time on the same day for the same staff member is not an overlap (touching intervals) and must be accepted.
A shift whose start time is greater than or equal to its end time (zero or negative duration) must be rejected as invalid input.
Adding a shift that brings weekly hours exactly equal to the staff cap is allowed; only strictly exceeding the cap warns and refuses.
Adding a shift that exceeds the weekly cap is accepted only when the override flag is true, and the stored/displayed shift reflects the override.
An appointment whose attendee count equals the room capacity is allowed; only strictly exceeding capacity is refused.
Two appointments in the same room that only touch at a boundary (startA == endB) are not a double-booking and must both be accepted.
An inactive staff member or inactive room must not be selectable for new shifts/appointments, while existing records referencing them remain visible.
Empty schedule data produces an empty conflict list and zero weekly hours without errors.
Two hard conflicts involving the same entry are both listed, each naming both offending entries.
A time-off request that is still Requested (not Approved) does not create a shift-overlap conflict; only Approved time off is flagged.
An approved time-off range that partially overlaps a shift (overlap on either end) and one that fully contains/abuts a shift are each flagged when the overlap rule holds.
A denied time-off request still appears in the staff view; a request spanning week boundaries is matched to shifts by the overlap rule, not by containment.
Approving a time-off request that overlaps an existing shift is permitted but must appear in the conflict detector afterward.
Simultaneous/concurrent add attempts for the same staff-day or same room-time must not both persist conflicting entries; the second is refused naming the first.
Duplicate identical bookings submitted twice must result in one persisted entry with the second refused as a conflict naming the first.
Keyboard navigation through the grid rows/cells works without a pointer, and the grid exposes table/grid roles with labelled time inputs.
errorHandling: Invalid input (missing staff, room, date, or non-integer/out-of-range minute values, or start >= end) returns a validation failure naming the offending field and persists nothing.
An overlapping staff shift refusal returns the message naming the specific conflicting shift entry and does not mutate stored schedule data.
A weekly-cap exceedance refusal returns a warning stating the projected weekly hours and the cap, and persists nothing unless the override flag is set.
A room double-booking refusal names the specific conflicting appointment and persists nothing.
An attendee-count-over-capacity refusal states the requested count and the room capacity and persists nothing.
A denied or approved time-off decision requires a note; a decision with an empty note is rejected without changing status.
A local persistence read failure surfaces an explicit load error rather than silently showing an empty schedule.
A local persistence write failure is reported and the in-memory/stored state is not left in a partially written state.
Requesting time off for a staff member with an already-pending overlapping request is reported as a conflict rather than silently duplicated.

dataFlow: Manager opens the weekly rota view; the app loads persisted ScheduleData (staff, rooms, shifts, appointments, timeOffRequests) locally, and a load failure surfaces an explicit error.
Manager adds a shift by selecting staff, date, start minute, and end minute; inputs are validated for presence, integer minute range, and start < end.
The new shift is tested against the same staff member's same-day shifts via startA < endB && startB < endA; on overlap the flow stops and names the conflicting shift.

The projected weekly hours are computed by summing that staff's shift durations for the Monday–Sunday week and compared to the staff cap; on exceedance without the override flag the flow stops with a warning.
On success the shift (with its override flag) is appended to the schedule and saved via local persistence; a write failure is reported without leaving a partial write.
Reception books an appointment by selecting title, room, date, start, end, booked-by, and attendee count; validation checks capacity and then checks room overlap with existing appointments.
On capacity exceedance or room overlap the flow stops and names the capacity or the conflicting appointment; otherwise the appointment is persisted locally.
Staff view selects a staff member and reads that member's shifts for the current week plus all their time-off requests, showing approved and denied.
A staff member requests time off (staff, start date, end date, note); it is persisted with status Requested.
Manager decides a time-off request by setting status Approved or Denied with a required note; an empty note stops the flow without changing status.

The conflict detector scans the week's shifts, appointments, and approved time-off requests, collecting double-booked rooms, overlapping staff shifts, and shift-overlapping-approved-time-off, each naming both entries.
All conflict, overlap, and hours computations run as pure functions over ScheduleData and are reused by both the rota builder and the conflict detector before any UI rendering.
